title: Milan: treadmill incline steady
terrain: treadmill 8-10% incline, climbing only, zero descent
coachNotes: FUELLING TARGET RAISED 60 -> 80 g/h ON 24 AUG. THIS SUPERSEDES EVERY 60 g/h TARGET BELOW. Products checked: Enervit Carbo Gel C2:1 Pro is 40g of carbohydrate per 60ml gel at a 2:1 glucose-fructose ratio, roughly double a normal gel, and the fructose clears the single-transporter ceiling that set the old 60 target. SiS GO Isotonic is 22g and maltodextrin only, i.e. glucose pathway only, 10mg sodium. GUT TRAINING ON ANY RUN OVER AN HOUR: 2 Enervit gels per hour, one on the hour and one on the half hour. WATER IS NOT OPTIONAL WITH THESE GELS: 40g in 60ml is about a 66% solution, strongly hypertonic, and taken dry it pulls water into the gut. 150-250ml of water with every gel. Do not stack a SiS gel on top of 2 Enervit, it is glucose only and pushes you past the ~60 g/h glucose ceiling without adding fructose. Transporter capacity adapts over roughly two weeks of repeated exposure, so this starts now or it does not happen before 5 September. Today is 50 minutes, just under the hour, so take one gel at minute 30 anyway to keep the exposure going. Climbing strength with no eccentric cost, which is the whole argument for a treadmill in a flat week. Hold the incline and let the pace be whatever it needs to be, the gradient is the prescription and the speed is not. This is also race-pace climbing effort, so learn what 80-88% feels like when it is boring. GUT TRAINING: 60 g/h from minute 30, on this run too. Transporter capacity adapts over about two weeks of repeated exposure, so the adaptation either starts now or it does not happen before 5 September. Put carbohydrate in the bottle rather than trying to chew your way there. No gym today, legs recover between Tuesday and Thursday.
